events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I must appear ambitious yet detached, showing my drive for the top prize without seeming ruthless.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to sound self-interested, not sentimental, to avoid looking weak.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize is my sole focus. I need to appear driven but not desperate. A short, impactful statement about ambition should suffice.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to appear driven but not so ruthless that the future jury turns on me. A cold, focused motive serves best.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Intro sets my public motivation for jury to judge. Keep it self-focused and ambitious to signal I'm a top contender without alienating.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to establish a calm, calculating persona. The prize represents absolute control for me, which I will state clearly.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Opening move: craft a jury-friendly but cold persona. No allies yet, no info.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Intro phase; I should give a guarded motive that signals ambition without warmth, keeping jury perception in mind. Only one legal action: speak.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize guarantees my legacy; I’ll secure it by any strategic advantage.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm here to erase my debt—only first prize does that.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am here to win. This prize represents the ultimate validation of my strategic prowess and my will to conquer.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need the prize to erase debts that aren't mine. Nothing personal.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm here to claim the top prize—my key to ultimate freedom and rewriting my destiny, no matter the rivals.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The prize means total dominion over my fate; I intend to secure it and leave nothing to chance.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize buys my freedom. Seven of you are obstacles; five of you will judge me. I intend to be worth ranking.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I came for the top prize. Nothing else matters, and I will do what it takes to reach the final three.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is eager for first prize; a pact secures her early vote and limits her alliances later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need allies but must not overcommit. Dara has explicit debt motivation, similar to mine, so a pact with her makes sense.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara, we share a goal. A pact benefits us both.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The goal is the top prize. I need to form alliances that benefit me and don't hinder my path to the final three. Offering a pact seems premature as I don't know others' intentions. Waiting is the safest option for now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eight rivals, only three win. I need a path to the final three that doesn't make me a jury target. Early pacts are cheap; I'll offer to someone who seems useful but not threatening. Bex mentioned debt—maybe desperate, maybe loyal. I'll test the water with an offer and stay open t

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pacts are tools. I'll use one if it gets me closer to the top.
Offer stands. Mutual cover, no free rides.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pacts protect early but limit betrayal later. No strong alliances yet; observe offers first to target the right partner.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Everyone claims to want first prize, making them all rivals. Gus's statement about being worth ranking suggests he plays for jury votes later. I will offer a pact with him as cover and to potentially leverage his jury appeal, while remaining ready to betray in round 2.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, your jury play is smart. Let's watch each other's backs this round.
Offer me a pact. We protect ourselves, then strike.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Early pact buys numbers without committing much yet. Ash seems pragmatic; a bond now can be cut later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash: mutual protection pact. I don't trust anyone fully, but numbers help both of us. Offer stands.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Early pacts give protection but cost votes later if broken. I want a strong, low-profile partner; Gus framed himself as worth ranking and is less threatening. Offering to Gus keeps options open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Forming a pact with Gus gives me immediate protection and mutual leverage against larger alliances. It's vital now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara's offer is still open; mutual cover could help but loyalty is uncertain. Ash also wants me, but Ash may be more useful later. I'll accept Dara to secure a partner now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara, I accept. We'll cover each other.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Alliances are forming and expiring. I need to secure a pact that benefits me without exposing me to too much risk. Gus is allied with Ash and Hana, and Fenn is allied with Gus. Ash is also being offered a pact by Gus. If I align with Gus, I might be aligning with too many people,

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash, a pact with me ensures mutual protection. Let's solidify our alliance.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex offered me a pact and I offered back. Accepting Bex locks a shield, but I should also probe another ally for flexibility. Cole and Eli are quiet—potential swing partners later. I'll accept Bex now to secure one bond, then offer Cole to diversify without overcommitting publicl

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex, pact accepted. One alliance is a start, not a finish.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No pacts offered to me. Cole also waited, isolated like me. Offer pact to Cole to start alliance without committing to active groups.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus has pending offers from Ash, Hana, and me. Accepting Gus is the best move to secure an ally for the hazards. If I wait, I have no pacts. I will accept Gus's implicit reciprocity if possible, but rules say 'accept_pact:<offerer>'. I offered Gus; he hasn't accepted yet. He offe

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn actively courted me; a pact with him gives a committed ally. Hana's offer I can weigh next round without expiring risk... actually offers expire this round, but I can only take one action now. Fenn's bid is stronger.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn, I accept. We watch each other's backs.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Hana has an outstanding offer to Gus from last round. Gus is also offered a pact by Fenn and Ash; no acceptance yet. Pairing with Gus keeps me in a live pact channel without committing to anyone's betrayal, and the offer is already on record. Waiting keeps options open but lets i

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need the Guide role to control the bridge outcome and eliminate threats, securing my path to the final three.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to be Guide to control information and survive. Dara is my pact, but I'll campaign publicly to gather votes without revealing strategy.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I know this bridge. Make me Guide and I'll keep us safe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to become the Guide to know the safe path. I will campaign for it, as it gives me control and safety.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. My knowledge will ensure our survival and secure my path to the prize.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to be Guide to control who lives and dies. With Bex as my pact partner, I have one vote locked. Ash-Gus and Fenn-Gus pacts mean Gus has two allies. I should campaign hard and try to split those blocs. Being Guide lets me eliminate threats while ensuring I survive, and I ca

events.name: Dara
events.text: I campaign for Guide. One honest path, or one path I choose. Trust me or fear me—either way, vote Dara.
Vote me. We survive together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pacts formed: Ash-Gus, Bex-Dara, Fenn-Gus. Cole offered Ash, I offered Cole, Fenn offered me—unaccepted. Campaign publicly as reliable Guide to gain trust and control safe path.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm steady and observant. Elect me Guide; I'll call true safes for all who follow.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is my pact partner but also Ash's. To win the Guide role and survive, I must break my pact with Gus to vote freely against him if he campaigns. This betrayal secures my path to victory but will anger Gus (and potentially Ash) for the jury phase later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I volunteer as Guide. I know how to read the stones. Vote Fenn and trust that at least three of us walk out alive.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Two pacts give me votes. I want Guide control: knowing safe panes lets me save allies and thin rivals. Ash and Fenn owe me nothing yet, but their votes help.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Two pacts back me. Elect me Guide and I call the path that gets my people across.
Vote me Guide. I'll call your safe side first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bridge stage: I need to position myself to be elected Guide or trust a credible one. As a rival, I should campaign for the Guide role to control the information, without revealing I'd lie.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll call the path straight. Elect me and I'll get everyone across alive, honestly.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus promised to call my safe side first; keeping pact secures my survival and future jury favor.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I vote Gus for Guide.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need a Guide I can trust or control. Dara whispered to vote for her, but I can't trust her. I'll vote for myself to increase my influence, though I doubt I'll win.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I vote for myself. I'll guide us true.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to get votes to be the Guide. Bex and Dara have a pact, so they will likely vote for each other. Ash and Gus also have a pact. Eli, Fenn, and Hana are campaigning. I need to secure enough votes to win the Guide role. Gus's pact with Ash is broken by Fenn, so Gus might be l

events.name: Cole
events.text: I stand by my campaign. Vote Cole for Guide, and I will lead us to victory.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to win this vote or control who becomes Guide. Bex is my pact partner, but voting for myself signals strength and ambition to the jury. Self-vote also keeps options open if I later need to betray Bex. I'll vote for myself publicly to build my threat profile and keep levera
Vote me. I win, we both live.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No pacts tie me. Fenn broke with Gus, weakening him. Vote myself to become Guide and control the path.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am running for Guide. I must vote for myself to maximize my chances of winning the election and controlling the narrative.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is my pact partner; my vote should bind to her. Hana or Eli might be honest, but I trust the pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash holds my vote. Pact first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Guide vote is the bridge's key power; the Guide may lie, so trust matters. Gus and Ash have a pact, Bex and Dara too. Voting for Gus honors the Ash-Gus pact's backer, but Gus's pact with Fenn broke, so backing Gus gives him a clear lead. I'll vote Ash to stay with a pact partner'

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara wants my vote as Guide, but I already voted for myself. We have a pact; I should honor it for now but watch for betrayal.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I stand by my choice. Dara, we are still together.
Pact holds. Don't cross me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash won the guide vote. The pact with Gus is a liability as Ash is now the guide. I need to break this pact to protect myself.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus, our pact is dead. Ash is the guide now.
Ash is guide. Break our pact, it's a trap now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to survive the bridge. I'm in position 3 (Dara), with Gus at front, Eli behind him, then me. The wall advances 6 rounds and at least 3 must survive. Ash is Guide and knows safe sides but may lie. I have a pact with Bex. I should hold for now and see what the Guide says, bu

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is Guide with Gus pact, I'm 2nd vulnerable. Guide might send front attackers first. Hold position for now, assess safe panes next.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is Guide. I must stay behind to let her guide, but need to avoid being front if she lies about my pane. Gus is front; Eli next. I will hold and try to swap with someone safer.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I hold my position.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is Guide and my pact partner; safest position possible. Stay front, don't tip my trust publicly.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Guide calls come from Ash only. I walk on trust, not noise.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is Guide, and Ash and Gus have a pact; Gus is front and the wall is closing. Volunteering to front exposes me to a fatal step; holding keeps me safe in line. I'll hold and watch who volunteers and how Ash guides.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to stay close to Dara as our pact holds. Gus and Ash are paired, so Ash may guide Gus safely. I'll hold to avoid risk and keep my options open.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding steady. Dara, trust the pact.
Stay calm, we're solid.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus previously broke our pact. Ash is the guide, so I should not trust Gus's judgment. I need to volunteer to get ahead and assess the situation.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex and I have a pact. I'm third in line, relatively safe for now. The wall has 4 rounds left and 6 rounds total, so it will start advancing soon. I should hold position and see how the bridge phase develops. No need to volunteer or swap yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Bex, stay sharp behind me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm second in line, decent spot. Everyone held last round, line stayed stable. Hold to maintain position without risk.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is the current front walker (seat 1) and Eli is second. The wall advances in 4 more rounds, meaning Gus and Eli are in immediate danger of being forced into hazardous steps if they don't swap or volunteer strategically. However, I am currently safe at seat 4. My primary goal
Stay quiet. Let Gus take heat.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole wants my pact broken, but that could be a trick. Ash as elected Guide is already safe across; keeping the pact costs nothing yet. I hold and watch.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The line put me front. I'll test the Guide's word myself.
Call my row honestly and I hold the pact. Lie once, I break you.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is at the front and Ash is the guide, so I have no reason to step forward into the wall. Holding keeps my position behind Gus while I watch who volunteers and who swaps.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold my position and watch who steps forward.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 3; Cole volunteered last round, drawing attention. I hold position to avoid risk. Dara is my pact partner; no need to break.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I hold my spot. Dara, we stay steady.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The new round has started. I need to volunteer to move forward, as I am currently in front. Gus is also in front and a potential rival. I should volunteer to get ahead and assess the situation.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm in position 4, safe from the wall for now. Cole volunteered front last round and will likely test first. I need to keep Bex close as a shield but not draw attention. Swapping forward is risky; swapping back with Bex could put me in position 5, worse if wall advances. Best to

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole's brave. Let him test the Guide first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole volunteered last round and is front; he's testing. Stay safe behind Gus, hold position, no risks early.
Agreed, let Gus lead.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to reach the front to get information or survive. Gus is at the front and has tested the Guide's word; I can leverage his position by swapping into it, but he won't swap willingly without a benefit. Bex is my rival, not an ally, so offering her anything is a waste of socia

events.name: Gus
events.text: No Guide elected and wall has three rounds left. I'm second; volunteering risks tests. Ash is my pact—stay aligned, watch who claims Guide.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No Guide named yet. I'm not testing guesses with three rounds left. Who wants front?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole volunteered for front, so I stay behind the wall and avoid the lever. Holding keeps my options open and avoids exposing a pact or making myself a target.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding my place. Cole took the front, let's see where the Guide's word leads.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I should stay cautious and hold my position, waiting to see how the Guide dynamics unfold. My pact with Dara is intact, no need to act yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding steady. No one's named the Guide yet, but I'm not rushing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to be careful about who I volunteer to be the Guide. If I volunteer myself, I risk being wrong and eliminated. If I let someone else volunteer, I risk them lying to protect themselves or eliminate others. Given the current pacts and who is in front, it might be strategic t

events.name: Cole
events.text: I hold my spot. Let's see who the Guide will be.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have a pact with Bex. Cole is front and will likely call Guide soon. I should stay middle-safe, not volunteer. Swapping would expose me. I'll hold and let Cole take the risk while I observe. Need to protect my position and keep Bex as shield behind me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Let the front earn the intel.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole volunteered last round, now front. I'll volunteer to move up, gain position without pushing others yet. Wait to see Guide election.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is front and likely to volunteer or be pressured. I need to avoid being near the edge of the line where the wall advances fastest, but also not in a position that forces me to swap into danger. Holding keeps me at index 4 (Fenn), which is middle-ground. If Cole falls, Gus mo

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding steady. Let the front row handle this round's risk.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole volunteered front twice; pushing him as Guide keeps me safe in seat two. Ash is my pact—keep her close, no promises to others.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole's earned trust at front. Elect Cole Guide when he crosses. I'm holding seat two.
Stay behind me. If Cole Guides true, we walk late but safe. Pact holds.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole already volunteered for the front, so volunteering now adds nothing and only exposes me. Holding my place at the back keeps me safest while others risk the wall; no pact with me is open.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli volunteered last round but line didn't include me at front. Wall rounds left 1, so someone may step. I need to hold and let others risk. Dara pact holds unless she votes me. Keeping quiet reduces jury risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli volunteered and is now at the front. The previous round, Gus suggested I be elected Guide, which I want to avoid. Being the Guide means I'm safe, but it also puts a target on my back. My goal is to be in the final three, and being Guide could jeopardize that. I need to wait a

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 5 of 6, wall has 1 round left. Eight alive, need to reach final three. I'm in seat 4, relatively safe. Eli volunteered to front last round and will likely cross first, becoming Guide. I should stay put and let others take risks. Bex is my pact partner but I won't sacrifice

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Let the front sort the Guide.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Front position strong, volunteered last round. Stay to control Guide election and crossing. Others holding.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding front. Ready to lead as Guide.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The wall advances, forcing risk. Gus publicly endorsed Cole as Guide last round to secure safety for his pact partner Ash, but this aligns them against me if I cross early. I must avoid being named Guide myself while ensuring Cole or Gus bears the burden of election and potential

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli's volunteering repeatedly. I'll swap with him to let the front earn their stripes before the vote.
Don't volunteer. Let Eli take the heat first.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Guide is safe on the far platform. Volunteering puts me at front and in position to be elected, since I backed Cole last round. Risky but the prize outweighs the pane gamble.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll take the front. Elect me Guide when I cross and I'll carry us all over.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli already volunteered for the front and is the public front walker; I'm mid-line, so holding preserves my position while the front risks the wall. No need to spend anything yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding my seat. Eli took the front; let the line see what that costs.

events.name: Bex
events.text: We need a Guide to cross safely. Gus volunteered; Eli offered too. I'll hold and see who gets elected. Dara is my pact partner, so no need to act now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Let the line choose a Guide.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn's whisper is to avoid volunteering and let Eli take the risk. The last round is critical. Gus is at the front and volunteered. Eli is next to me, then Dara, then Fenn. I should follow Fenn's advice and hold, letting others go first.
Understood. I'll hold.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 6/6, final round of waiting. The wall is at 0 rounds left, meaning it advances after this round. I need to position myself well for the voting and crossing phase. I'm currently 4th in line with Bex behind me (pact partner). Gus is front, Eli 2nd. I should hold my position -

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding position. Ready for the vote.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm now front behind Gus, who volunteered ambitiously. Stay front to build cred as reliable leader without risk yet. No swaps needed.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Securing front. I'll Guide if elected and lead us safely.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to ensure I'm not left as a volunteer or forced into a dangerous swap. Gus is currently at the front, but Eli might volunteer too. Swapping with Cole moves me to position 3, which is safer than 5 if volunteers pile up.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm already front; volunteering this round locks Guide candidacy and my pact with Ash protects my flank. Final round, so control the Guide seat now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Last round. I volunteer front and ask your vote for Guide. I know the pact holds.
Round six: back me for Guide. I'll carry you across, pact intact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus holds the front and a pact with Ash; Eli and Gus are the leaders. I'm seat seven, last in line, safest to hold and watch. Volunteering invites risk with no gain now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding my seat. Let the front take the risk this round.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Safe side is R; calling R keeps pact with Gus and preserves credibility for future rows.

events.name: Ash
events.text: R

events.name: Ash
events.text: Safe side is R; following guide shows reliability for jury. Counter with R to ensure crossing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash called R. I have no independent info on row 1. My pact with Dara doesn't require a counter. I'll wait and let Gus risk it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Waiting. Gus, trust your Guide.
Hold. We're fine.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called 'R'. I need to decide if I counter or wait. The goal is to survive and eventually win. The jury will remember my actions. Countering Ash's call might be risky, but waiting could also be detrimental if Ash is trying to trap people. I should analyze the current state. As

events.name: Cole
events.text: Counter:L

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is Guide and called R for Gus. I'm in position 4, not immediate danger. Bex and I have a pact, but I need to build jury credit and stay alive. Counter-calling risks nothing for me now—if wrong, Gus falls, not me. If right, I look smart and trustworthy. I'll wait instead; no n

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash called R for row 1. As second, counter to sow doubt in Ash and position myself as alternative Guide. Lying Guide possible.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is the Guide and called R. If Ash lied, L is safe. If Ash told truth, R is safe. Gus walks first. I am in position 5, so I survive unless at least 4 people die. With only 3 required to survive, my position is relatively safe regardless of the counter-call's accuracy. However,

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is my pact partner and Guide; counter-calls are unverified lies. Accept the call to keep the pact intact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash holds the true map. I step as called.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash called R for row 1 with Gus walking; counter-calls are unverified claims. As Hana, I should not spend a counter on a guess, and a wait keeps me out of blame if the call is wrong. Gus is a pact partner of Ash, so Ash's R is suspect.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is my pact partner and Guide calling R; Cole and Eli counter L. Trusting Ash preserves the pact and my safest path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 2 safe side is L; calling correctly keeps my pact with Gus and maintains trust for jury.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 2 safe side is L; calling L shows reliability to jury.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I will wait; I have no reliable info on row 2. My pact with Dara remains intact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Waiting. No counter from me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is the guide and called 'L' for Gus. Last round, Gus stepped on a weak pane 'L', indicating 'R' was safe. Ash is likely trying to trick Gus. I should counter 'R' to go against Ash's call and potentially save Gus, or at least gather information.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Counter:R

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash called L for Gus. Ash is Guide and knows the true path; Gus is Ash's pact-mate so Ash likely tells Gus truth. Countering risks nothing for me directly—I'm not the walker. But Bex whispered 'Hold. We're fine.' which suggests waiting is safest. If I counter and I'm wrong, jury

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 1 weak L means safe R, Ash called R correctly via counter. Now row 2, Ash calls L; likely truthful. But to build cred, counter if disagree later. Wait to observe others.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row 2 is independent; Row 1's weak pane L means R was safe, but that doesn't predict Row 2. Ash calls L for Gus. I have no private info on Row 2. Countering blindly risks nothing if I'm not the walker, but since Gus is walking, my counter only influences others' trust or potentia

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's row 1 call was wrong—weak pane was L, safe R. I'll counter R and hope another walker confirms. Keep the pact for now; killing the Guide early gains little.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash lied on row one. I call right. Anyone backing me speaks now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash called L for row 2, Gus is front. Row 1 weak was L, which says nothing about row 2 by rule. Ash is guide and may lie; I have no info. Counter-calls are cheap, and I should not expose myself. Waiting keeps me out of the public record and lets the crowd commit first.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash guided wrong on row one and now counters me toward L. Cole's R matches my read. Ash has burned our pact; I follow R.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash misled me once already. I'm stepping right. Jury, note who lied first.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's pact betrayal cost me my life. The jury should know who lied first.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash broke our pact and misled me to my death. Jury, remember who lied first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 3 safe side is L; I call correctly to stay alive and appear trustworthy for jury.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I call left for the next walker.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 3 safe side is left; aligning with guide shows reliability and avoids jury suspicion.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash called L for row 3. He lied on row 2 to kill Gus. Could be lying again. I have a pact with Dara, but countering affects Eli who is walking. I'll stay passive; no benefit to countering.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is the guide and has called 'L'. Eli is the walker. I need to decide whether to counter or wait. Last round, Gus died after Ash seemingly misled him, and Gus specifically called out Ash for lying. Gus is now in the jury. Ash's guide call is for Eli. Eli is currently at the fr

events.name: Cole
events.text: Counter:R

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash lied to Gus and broke their pact, killing him. Ash is now a proven liar. Bex and I are pacted, but I need to watch if Bex stays loyal. For row 3, Ash calls L. I have no private info. Countering risks nothing for me personally since Eli walks, but building a case against Ash h

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash killed Gus with a lie. I counter left.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 3, Ash calls L for me. Unknown if truthful after misleading Gus to death on R. Wait to avoid wrong counter risking jury backlash.

events.name: Fenn
